# src/ — The Four Clean Architecture Projects

This directory holds the four projects that make up the backend, one per Clean Architecture layer. See `../ARCHITECTURE.semantic.md` for the system-level picture; this file covers what's actually implemented in each project today.

## Why four projects, not four folders in one project

Separate assemblies make the dependency rules compiler-enforced in one specific way: a circular reference between projects fails `dotnet restore`/`dotnet build` outright (see the `../tests/.semantic.md` section on the cycle experiment). Folders within a single project wouldn't give that guarantee — nothing would stop `Domain.cs` from calling into `Infrastructure.cs` if they shared an assembly.

## TutoringCentre.Domain

Empty. No business entities exist yet. References nothing — not even a NuGet package beyond the SDK defaults. Contains only `AssemblyMarker.cs`, an empty internal class that exists purely so architecture tests can get a handle on this assembly via `typeof(AssemblyMarker).Assembly` (a compile-time-checked way to load an assembly, instead of a string-based `Assembly.Load("...")` that would fail silently on a typo).

## TutoringCentre.Application

Also empty of business logic. Has one real file: `DependencyInjection.cs`, which defines `AddApplication(this IServiceCollection services)` — currently a no-op that just returns `services`, waiting for future use cases to register themselves here. References Domain only.

**Why this file exists even though it does nothing yet**: it establishes the pattern every layer follows — each layer owns a single `AddXxx(IServiceCollection)` extension method that registers everything that layer needs, so `Program.cs` never has to know the internals of any layer. It only calls `.AddApplication().AddInfrastructure(configuration)`.

## TutoringCentre.Infrastructure

The one project with real logic right now. Two files:

- **`AssemblyMarker.cs`** — same purpose as Domain's: lets architecture tests load this assembly by type instead of by string.
- **`DependencyInjection.cs`** — defines `AddInfrastructure(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration)`, which registers the PostgreSQL readiness health check:
  1. Reads `configuration.GetConnectionString("Postgres")`.
  2. If that string is null or empty, registers a health check named `"postgres"` (tag `"ready"`) that **always reports `Unhealthy`** with the message `"ConnectionStrings:Postgres is not configured."` — deliberately, so a missing connection string degrades readiness instead of throwing an exception during app startup.
  3. If the string is present, registers the real check via `AddNpgSql(connectionString, name: "postgres", tags: ["ready"])`, which the `AspNetCore.HealthChecks.NpgSql` package implements by pinging the database.

References Application and Domain (it implements the kind of interfaces Application would define, even though Application doesn't define any yet — this is Dependency Inversion in miniature: the health-check *contract* is provided by `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks`, and Infrastructure supplies the concrete Postgres-specific implementation).

**Package note**: `AspNetCore.HealthChecks.NpgSql` is referenced *only* here, never by Api. This is intentional and checked by `DependencyRuleTests.Infrastructure_DoesNotDependOnApi` and, more directly, by the fact that Npgsql-specific code simply doesn't exist anywhere in `TutoringCentre.Api`.

## TutoringCentre.Api

The ASP.NET Core host — the composition root and the only place that assembles all the layers together. `Program.cs`:

1. Calls `builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()` — registers the core health-check infrastructure (needed even before any specific check is added, because `MapHealthChecks` needs it to exist).
2. Calls `builder.Services.AddApplication().AddInfrastructure(builder.Configuration)` — the one line where Api "knows about" the other layers, purely to wire them into DI.
3. Maps `GET /health` with `Predicate = _ => false` — liveness, runs zero checks, always `200 Healthy` while the process is alive.
4. Maps `GET /health/ready` with `Predicate = c => c.Tags.Contains("ready")` — readiness, runs only checks tagged `"ready"` (today: just Postgres).
5. `public partial class Program;` at the end — top-level statements implicitly generate an `internal` `Program` class; this explicit `public partial` declaration makes it `public` so `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` in the test project can host it in-process (see `../tests/.semantic.md`).

References Application and Infrastructure. The Infrastructure reference exists *only* for step 2 above — endpoint code must never import an Infrastructure type directly (see `../ARCHITECTURE.semantic.md`, "Why the Api → Infrastructure reference is dashed").

Configuration: `appsettings.json` declares `ConnectionStrings:Postgres` with an empty string (documents the key without committing a real value); the project has a `UserSecretsId` so the real local connection string lives in `dotnet user-secrets`, never in a committed file.

## Important files

| File | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| `TutoringCentre.Api/Program.cs` | Composition root; where the two health endpoints are mapped |
| `TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` | The only non-trivial logic in `src/` today — Postgres health check wiring |
| `TutoringCentre.Application/DependencyInjection.cs` | The no-op pattern every layer's DI entry point follows |
| `*/AssemblyMarker.cs` (all four) | Lets architecture tests reference each assembly by type, not by string |

## Edge cases and gotchas

- **Don't add `Npgsql` or `AddNpgSql` to `Program.cs`.** If this ever happens, `DependencyRuleTests` won't catch it directly (it only checks Domain/Application/Infrastructure, not Api), but it would defeat the point of the layering — Api should never know Postgres exists beyond calling `AddInfrastructure`.
- **A missing/empty `ConnectionStrings:Postgres` is a valid, supported state** — it should make `/health/ready` return 503, not throw an unhandled exception. Don't "fix" this by adding strict startup validation here (that's planned for a later task, per the ADR's roadmap).
- **Each project's `.csproj` intentionally omits `TargetFramework`/`Nullable`/`ImplicitUsings`** — those are set once in `../Directory.Build.props` and would silently drift if duplicated per-project with a different value.
